gaps: T1 lists `ChapterCard.module.css` and a 'ChapterCard root' in the approach narrative, but no `ChapterCard` component exists in the repo — `frontend/app/series/[id]/_components/ChapterList.tsx` renders chapters inline. The plan must either drop the ChapterCard reference or specify the exact element (an `<a>` inside ChapterList.module.css) that should carry `data-dock-item`.

T1 mentions removing `:hover { transform: translateY(-2px) }` from StoryCard.module.css and ContinueCard.module.css, but does NOT mention `ContinueReadingRow.module.css` line 67-68 (`.card:hover { transform: translateY(-2px) }`) — that file IS in `filesToChange` but the CSS conflict it shares with the dock hook is not enumerated. SeriesCard reuses StoryCard.module.css, so removing the hover translateY there silently removes it from SeriesCard as well — that side effect is not flagged.

T1 fails to list `frontend/components/ChapterList.module.css`, `frontend/components/SeriesCard.module.css` (if separate), or globals.css `--transition-fast` — the per-card `transition: transform var(--transition-fast)` rule on `.card` in StoryCard.module.css will fight every per-frame GSAP write. The risks section calls this out but the `filesToChange` list does not say which lines/properties to scope to `border-color, box-shadow` only.

T1 does not name the integration point for the homepage hero rewrite: `frontend/app/page.tsx` is a server component (it exports `metadata`), so introducing a `'use client'` wrapper requires a NEW client component file (e.g. `frontend/app/_components/HeroCardsList.tsx`) — the plan says 'extract a tiny `use client` wrapper' but lists only `app/page.tsx` and `app/page.module.css` as the touch points, with no new file created. This is a missing file in `filesToCreate`.

T1's NotesPanel attachment misses the mobile sheet codepath: when the panel is in fixed-position sheet mode (under 1100px) the `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` matchMedia gate correctly disables the effect on touch — but on a hybrid 1100px-wide touchscreen laptop the dock will activate over a panel that's also being swiped. No fallback discussed.

T1 omits `frontend/components/ChapterRow` / `ChapterList` analysis — the open question says 'probably should NOT get the dock effect (clarify)' but there's no explicit decision branch in the approach; if it IS excluded, the existing `:hover { transform }` rule there must stay; if it is INCLUDED, ChapterList.tsx and its CSS need to be in `filesToChange`. Plan is ambiguous on the actual edit.

T1 does not list the `frontend/components/InlineRichText` / `TagPill` subtree behaviour: cards contain nested links and pills that themselves have hover states. The hook attaches `pointermove` on the container — children pointer events will still fire on the inner `<TagPill>` which has its own hover styles; no mention of whether `pointer-events: none` is needed on inner decorative elements to keep the proximity computation stable when the cursor briefly passes over a pill at the card edge.

T2 fails to list `frontend/app/admin/_components/NotesPanel.module.css` in `filesToChange`. The panel-level `.panel { transition: max-height 260ms... }` and the `.hasExpanded { min-height: calc(100dvh - 90px); max-height: calc(100dvh - 90px) }` rules combine with the per-card `AutoHeightPanel` height tween: the per-card tween will be measuring its `getBoundingClientRect().height` while the parent panel is mid-transition, producing a wrong `fullH`. The plan calls this 'reconciling … only if needed' — but it WILL be needed and that's not in the DoD.

T2 says to remove `animation: noteExpandIn 200ms`, but doesn't address the per-card `transition: transform 180ms, box-shadow 220ms` on `.card` (NoteCard.module.css lines 18-22). The AutoHeightPanel wraps the body content but the .card itself still has a transform-y transition that the dock hook (T1) will write to — sequencing problem: T1 must remove the transform transition that T2 doesn't touch.

T2 plan to 'always render both branches' inside `<AutoHeightPanel open={expanded}>` will change NoteCard.tsx behavior significantly: title `<input>` and `<textarea>` will be mounted even when collapsed. That means autosave timers, `useEffect` for typing-to-PATCH (lines 76-95) and the menu's outside-click listener will all be running in every collapsed card. Performance + stale-write risk not flagged.

T2's reduced-motion plan calls `gsap.set(el, { height: open ? 'auto' : 0 })` but in the same component the GSAP path uses `overflow: 'hidden'` during tween — the reduced-motion path doesn't set overflow at all, so on the FIRST mount when collapsed, the user will see content overflow before the height collapses (no `overflow: hidden` on the 0-height collapsed state).

T3 has a factual error: it claims `onShareClick(target, i, e)` in `QuoteShare.tsx`, but the current signature is `onShareClick = async (target: ShareTarget, index: number)` — there is no event arg, and the call site passes `() => void onShareClick(target, i)` (no event). The plan's `gsap.fromTo(e.currentTarget, ...)` will not work without first widening the signature and updating the onClick to pass the event.

T3 references CSS token `--gold-soft` as a possible ShareButton flash color, but globals.css does NOT define `--gold-soft` — `frontend/app/globals.css` is not in `filesToChange` for T3 even though adding/defining the token belongs there. The open question is asked but no implementation path is sketched for whichever answer is chosen.

T3's CSS-variable-via-box-shadow trick relies on `color-mix(in oklab, …)` — browser support is fine on modern Chrome/Safari/Firefox but the existing codebase uses `color-mix(in srgb, …)` (see NoteCard.module.css line 44). Mixing color spaces between sibling button stylesheets is a tiny consistency risk not flagged. Also no `@property --pulse-flash` registration is planned — without it, the variable cannot be tweened numerically by GSAP through `box-shadow` interpolation; GSAP will tween the literal string. Risk acknowledged in passing ('keeps it live without needing @property') but this is GSAP-specific incorrect: GSAP's CSSPlugin tweens custom properties as numbers only when GSAP recognises a unitless number; you need `gsap.set(el, { '--pulse-flash': 0 })` to seed and the `--pulse-flash` won't animate smoothly without `@property` registration in modern browsers.

T3 does not say where the `useGSAP` scope is established for ShareButton — ShareButton currently has no `buttonRef` at all (only `copiedTimerRef`); the plan must add the ref AND set up `useGSAP({ scope: buttonRef })`. Same for SaveButton (no ref today). The approach mentions this for SaveButton but not explicitly for ShareButton.

T3 mentions QuoteShare's brand buttons immediately call `dismiss()` after `window.open` — but the popover unmount happens via setSelection(null) (not shown in plan); `useGSAP` cleanup will revert the in-flight `fromTo`, snapping the button back to scale 1 mid-tween. That visual jolt is not addressed.

T4 risk list mentions `html { scroll-behavior: smooth }` but the plan never explicitly grep'd / verified globals.css — I checked: no `scroll-behavior` declarations exist anywhere in `frontend/app/`, so the comment to 'add a warning in lib/gsap.ts' has nothing to defend against. However it would be valuable to also block per-element `scroll-behavior: smooth` on `html, body` — not in DoD.

T4 fails to mention that the `restore` closure currently has `cancelled` set inside the effect cleanup, but `tween.kill()` storage requires storing the tween into a ref or outer let outside the requestIdleCallback callback — the plan says 'store tween for cleanup' but doesn't name the storage mechanism. The current code structure makes this non-trivial: `tween` is created inside the rIC callback which fires AFTER the effect runs; you must close over a mutable ref from the outer scope. Not specified.

T4 does not handle the case where ScrollTrigger is already registered for in-view reveals and the page also tweens window scroll — ScrollTrigger needs to know about the programmatic scroll so it can fire its trigger callbacks correctly. `gsap.to(window, { scrollTo: …, onUpdate: () => ScrollTrigger.update() })` is the safe pattern; not in plan.

T4 does not address the interaction with the `pendingTimeoutRef` and the `onScroll` listener: the active GSAP scroll-tween will fire `scroll` events at every frame, triggering `onScroll → sendNow()` which throttles position writes. So restoring a position will immediately cause 100+ wasted writes during the 1.1s tween — and they'll write the SAME final position by the end. Should pause `onScroll` reporting until tween completes.

T5 missing file: `frontend/components/ContinueCard.tsx` and `frontend/components/ContinueReadingRow.tsx` are mentioned only as 'card roots' but not in `filesToChange` for T5 — yet they also appear on /search results when there's reading progress. Plan is unclear whether they receive `data-flip-id`.

T5 module-level `flipBridge` Map is a 'global side effect' that survives Hot Module Reload — React Fast Refresh will accumulate stale state during dev. No clearing strategy on HMR.

T5 `Flip.from` with `absolute: true` on a CSS Grid container with auto-fill / minmax tracks will yank items out of the grid flow; when those items come back, the grid may have repositioned its remaining tracks producing a 'reflow during animation' visual jump. The plan mentions `simple: true` only as a maybe — needs commitment.

Plan acknowledges this in T4's rationale but if T5 lands first the registration line must already accept multiple plugins. Sequencing risk: a rebase conflict in a single registerPlugin() call between the two PRs.

Cross-cutting: No mention of testing — repo presumably has Vitest/RTL; the plan has zero test-coverage strategy for the new `useDockProximity` hook, the `flipBridge`, or the `AutoHeightPanel`. Not in DoD for any task.

T1's `useDockProximity` adds another container-scoped ScrollTrigger-less hook — fine — but T5 will dispatch many `Flip.from` tweens that each create their own onEnter/onLeave child tweens; no explicit `kill()` on route-change beyond the bridge expiry.
strongPoints: Single canonical import surface via `frontend/lib/gsap.ts` is correctly re-used for both new plugin registrations (T4 ScrollToPlugin, T5 Flip) — keeps SSR-safe registration in one place.

Reduced-motion is addressed in every task with the project's existing `prefersReducedMotion()` helper, not a one-off matchMedia check, and the gating happens at hook-install time (not animation-time), which is the right granularity.
`useGSAP({ scope: ref })` is correctly used as the lifecycle primitive everywhere, matching the codebase's existing pattern in CardGrid/ExpandableSection/LikeButton.
